extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for or managing NIH grants (postdocs, early-career investigators, PIs, grant administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for NIH grant applicants and their institutional grants offices on timelines, JIT, paylines, transfer-of-award, overlap/duplication, budget rules, and interactions with Program Officers and Grants Management. Covers multiple mechanisms (R01, K99/K00, K23, F32, R35/MIRA, SBIR) and IC/Institute-specific processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal-year Notice of Award deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: NoAs for the current FY must be issued before September 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no specific timing for many funding decisions—decisions are made through August and awards (NoAs) must be issued before 9/30 for that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) communications as a signal
rubrics_metrics.description: A generally positive PO comment is a good sign; the PO would not risk your missing a submission cycle and would advise resubmission if there were reasonable doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven’t communicated with your PO and think you may be in range for select pay, contact them now for guidance on rebuttal, resubmission, and timeframes. PO is not involved in award processing and may not have final funding news, but they can advise on next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships bypass Council
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship mechanisms (e.g., F32, K awards where applicable) do not undergo Council review in the same way as some other mechanisms; timing and internal discussions still affect processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional submission of JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Your institution actually submits the JIT; you can upload materials, but the institution (GMS/AOR) must submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award will be based on your submitted (and approved by peer review) budget. Work with your grants management staff; they must submit JIT. Rapid response to JIT requests is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select pay / post-Council funding workflow (NCI example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding steps: Council needs to approve the possibility of funding; then IC leadership (e.g., NCI SPL) decides prioritization; paylist is created; then NoA can be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple sub-steps occur between these stages; after the larger list, internal program leadership prioritizes awards and grants management processes them. Many applications on the larger list will not ultimately be funded due to duplication, administrative issues, eligibility, or lack of remaining funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative processing timeline variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative processing (from JIT to award) can take anywhere from days to months and varies widely across ICs and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect delays due to appropriations timing, COVID-19 impact, staff availability, audits, or personal events. Generally, awards will be issued before Sept 30, but status may remain 'pending' for weeks/months. If you need to know to start spending, get confirmation (via AOR) that award is planned within 90 days for pre-award spending setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance required before consideration of administrative supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs do not accept all administrative supplements; an application/supplement must be accepted before it can be considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO pre-submission communication increases chances of acceptance. 'Accepted for Consideration' is a necessary step but does not guarantee funding; IC priorities and available funds matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and management of overlapping/duplicate funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial overlap between two potential awards must be eliminated; you cannot have two grants with overlapping aims funded simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If overlap exists, either adjust scope or withdraw one application. Institutions/funders will enforce elimination of duplication as a condition of award; failing to do so can require returning funds. Tell program staff transparently and follow PO/GMS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling pending external grants (NSF/Foundation) alongside NIH submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not preemptively withdraw a pending foundation/NSF grant simply because an NIH PO asks about potential overlap; foundations can be flexible and NSF PDs may work to adjust scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can inform external funders that if the other award is issued you will adjust scope or withdraw. Discuss with your NSF PD or foundation contact; avoid unnecessarily withdrawing and risking both awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDeA co-funding nomination variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Chances for IDeA co-funding depend on how many nominations your institute submits, submissions from other institutes, score, and geographic diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most institutes submit 2–4 nominations but only 1–2 may be funded; if yours is the only nomination from your institute chances improve. No fixed probability—many variables matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline stability late in FY and ESI considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines tend not to move late in the fiscal year, but ICs may fund additional Early Stage Investigators (ESIs) to meet numerical ESI goals even if outside the payline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect payline to be relatively stable late in the FY, though programmatic priorities (e.g., ESI quotas, IDeA co-funding) can alter final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of eRA Commons status changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Status labels like 'Council review completed' are technical and not necessarily terminal indicators of non-funding; status changes can be manual or skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume 'Council review completed' means not funded—applications often show that status before moving to 'Pending administrative review'. If status lingers, contact PO after reasonable waiting (e.g., after holidays) for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to PO questions about other funding/acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: When PO asks about other funding and whether you would accept the award, respond quickly and accurately—POs check for concurrent support, job changes, or other reasons an applicant might no longer be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely replies can preserve your chance; ICs check candidates they are considering to avoid funding duplicates or those who have left the applicant pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award spending and AOR/GMS communication
rubrics_metrics.description: To enable pre-award spending, the AOR may need official confirmation that you are within 90 days of award for institutional setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMS/AOR interactions may be required for administrative confirmations. Some GMS offices prefer communication via AOR rather than PI for certain official status questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget construction for subcontracts
rubrics_metrics.description: For subcontracts, NIH typically does not allow inflationary increases across years; institutions should build in a one-time cushion (e.g., 10%) and keep subcontract direct costs flat thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you add inflationary increases they will likely be cut during review/administrative processing. Plan with a cushion in the first year instead of year-to-year inflation increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget increases above $500K require PO agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If your requested budget jumps above $500K in any year, you need a PO agreement/approval (and may need to switch from modular to detailed budget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of IC rules regarding budget formats and prior approval for large-budget requests; failure to follow may complicate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for changing from single PI to MPI between submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Switching from single PI to MPI must be driven by science (e.g., reviewers noted missing critical expertise) rather than to add a big name or share funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the new PI will genuinely take equal leadership and how the other support of all PIs will be considered by the IC (heavy other support may reduce funding chances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision strategy when offered one of multiple overlapping funding mechanisms (e.g., MIRA vs R01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If asked to withdraw a pending R01 due to MIRA selection (or vice versa), follow PO instructions; you cannot keep both if there is scientific overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think long-term: MIRA may offer funding stability; withdrawing a requested overlapping application is appropriate to avoid causing extra work for study sections and to maintain good relationships with POs. If asked to withdraw, comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting PO vs Grants Management Specialist (GMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can advise on scientific/programmatic likelihood and next steps; GMS handles administrative processing. Some ICs/GMS prefer communication via the AOR for official queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact PO for status/timing questions and for advice about future submissions; use GMS/AOR channels for administrative status and setup. Respect institutional SOPs about who should contact GMS.
